cards.title: Previews are real fights
cards.text: Every ability's preview is now a small real fight set up for it: real enemies, no damage from nowhere.
cards.why: You said many weren't shown, were in the wrong situation, didn't change by tier, and heroes took invisible damage. Open a few in the Book (0.25.0) and mark what's still off.

parts.title: Real enemies
parts.text: Goblins, orcs, skeletons, archers, shamans, and a spider, hellhound and frost wolf for poison, burn and chill bites, all running their own brains: they walk up, swing, shoot and wind up. Every hit on a hero comes from something you can see (was 49 abilities, traits and trinkets with invisible damage).

parts.title: A scene per ability
parts.text: 22 kinds of scene: a group, shooters, casters, a hurt friend, a downed friend, a blow about to land, a corpse and more. The hero's own brain picks the moment, as in a run, in 1052 of 1080 loops. Wrong-situation previews: 35 to 0.

parts.title: Tiers
parts.text: Scenes are built for tier III (a second hurt friend, a wall, oil, a kill), so lower tiers visibly do less: one turret, then two. Still alike: 18 tiers that only change a number or a cooldown, or last longer than the loop.

parts.title: Not done yet
parts.text: The monster pages' previews still use the blue straw dummies, and Silenced has no preview yet. Next on my list.

cards.title: Monster pages too
cards.text: Monster and status previews now play against real heroes; every status comes from someone you can see.
cards.why: The last straw dummies are gone from the Book's monster pages. Silenced has its own preview now.
cards.details:
Before, every monster preview used blue straw dummies and 720 of them showed health lost to nothing. Now each move faces a small party of real heroes fighting back (held at range for charges, in a ring for slams, against a wall for the boar's crash), and a death move is set off by a hero visibly killing it.

Statuses build up on a hero's own blows (bursting on the third) or come from the ability that puts them on in a run.

Silenced: a choir sprite sings and mends; the Cleric's Smite staggers it, the crossed-out bubble shows, the song stops while its ring of shots still fires, then it sings again.

Still weak: 7 monster moves sometimes land on nobody (the heroes walk out of the zone, as they would in a run), and 24 slow ones take more than 2.5 s. Trinket and potion previews still use the old dummies; next on my list.
